title: Structure-Aligned vs Fixed-Token Updating Under Matched Budget
formal_question: Does structure-aligned memory updating (P1) outperform fixed-token updating (B5) at the exact same number of gradient updates and parameter budget?
expected_primary_comparison: P1 (SA-CMS, 3-level) vs B5 (Fixed-token CMS, 3-level) under controlled conditions: identical SmolLM2-135M frozen backbone, identical 5,314,752 parameters, identical 200 training samples, identical seeds (42, 43, 44), identical context-evicted evaluation set.

audit_findings.claim_in_round2_report: P2 achieves 0.828 F1 on Vietnamese QA vs B4 (0.640 F1), proving structure alignment improves semantic retention by +29.4%.
audit_findings.scientific_flaw: SEVERE RQ-DRIFT AND CONFLATION. P2 is a 3-level Gated Hybrid system (5.3M params + BM25 retrieval). B4 is a 1-level adapter (1.77M params, zero retrieval). Comparing P2 vs B4 conflates retrieval presence (+BM25), parameter count (5.3M vs 1.77M), and architectural levels (3-level vs 1-level). It provides ZERO scientific evidence for structure-aligned vs fixed-token update boundaries.

actual_phase4_statistical_test.pooled_datasets: QASPER (30 items) + LongHealth (60 items) across Seeds 42, 43, 44

audit_findings.scientific_conclusion: The hypothesis that structure-aligned updating outperforms fixed-token updating is NOT PROVEN on the controlled Phase 4 benchmark. The observed difference (mean delta = +0.0093) has a p-value of 0.4143 (t-test) and 0.8589 (Wilcoxon), with Cohen's d = 0.0865, which is statistically indistinguishable from null noise.
audit_findings.required_action: Strictly prohibit claiming RQ2 is 'proven' by P2 vs B4. Accurately report: At the 200-sample budget, P1 vs B5 showed no statistically significant difference (p=0.4143); full validation of structural boundary advantages requires the larger training corpus on the external RTX 3050 GPU.
